bookTitle: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis

facts.statement: Anna Coulling opens Chapter 11 by emphasizing that the financial market does not run on chance or luck; instead, like a battlefield, it operates strictly on probabilities and odds decoded through volume and price analysis.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: The market does not run on chance or luck. Like the battlefield, it runs on probabilities and odds.

facts.statement: Price congestion areas represent sideways consolidation zones where the market pauses to absorb supply or demand, serving as the natural spawning grounds where new trends and trend reversals are born.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: This is the power of the congestion phase – it is the spawning ground of trends and reversals.

facts.statement: Chapter 11 synthesizes Richard Wyckoff's three fundamental laws: Supply and Demand govern directional breakouts, Cause and Effect dictate that consolidation duration determines trend magnitude, and Effort vs. Result requires high volume to validate breakouts.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: Integration of Wyckoff's Three Laws: Supply and Demand, Cause and Effect, Effort vs. Result.

facts.statement: The chapter highlights specific price patterns developing during congestion: falling triangles (bearish), rising triangles (bullish), pennants (coiled springs storing explosive energy), and triple tops or bottoms (reversal patterns).

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: Falling Triangle, Rising Triangle, Pennant Pattern, Triple Top & Triple Bottom.

facts.statement: Traders should analyze three timeframes simultaneously (a fast chart, primary trading chart, and slow benchmark chart) to evaluate trend alignment, distinguishing low-risk trades with the dominant trend from higher-risk counter-trend trades.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: Multi-Timeframe Triangulation: Consists of a fast chart... primary trading chart... and benchmark/dominant chart.

facts.statement: Traders must never enter a breakout on low volume; a valid breakout requires a clean candle close with visible clear water beyond the congestion boundary backed by well-above-average, rising volume.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: Never enter a breakout on low volume. A valid breakout requires a clean candle close above/below the level accompanied by well above-average, rising volume.

facts.statement: Stop losses should always be placed behind natural market-built barriers—specifically below the lowest pivot low of the congestion zone for long trades, or above the highest pivot high for short trades.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: Stop loss placement should always be placed behind natural market barriers—specifically below the lowest pivot low of the congestion zone... or above the highest pivot high.

facts.statement: Positions should be exited when VPA signals extreme anomalies like hanging stars or shooting stars on high volume at key levels, when stopping volume appears, or when price breaks back through a congestion boundary against the trade.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: Trade exit triggers: exit positions when VPA signals extreme anomalies... when stopping/topping-out volume appears, or when price breaks back through a congestion boundary.

facts.statement: On a GBP/USD 15-minute chart, a 70-candle congestion phase broke out following an RPI economic news release that drove price through resistance on massive volume validation, spawning a sustained bullish trend.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: GBP/USD 15-Minute Chart (Fig 11.10): A 70-candle congestion phase bounded by pivot highs and lows. An economic news release (RPI data) acted as the catalyst, driving price through resistance on massive volume.

facts.statement: On a GBP/USD 1-hour chart, a 4-day congestion phase developed a hanging man candle on high volume signaling weakness, followed by a wide-spread breakdown candle through support where the broken floor converted into resistance.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: GBP/USD 1-Hour Chart (Fig 11.11): A 4-day congestion phase defined by clear pivot highs... A hanging man candle on high volume signaled weakness, followed by a wide-spread breakdown candle through support.

facts.statement: Coulling compares price congestion areas to salmon spawning headwaters where new trends and reversals are born before breaking out into active directional movement.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: Salmon Spawning: Price congestion areas act as the 'spawning grounds' where new trends and reversals are born.

facts.statement: Technical pivot points act like an automated GPS visual plotter on a boat for quick convenience, whereas pure price action and volume serve as traditional map-and-compass navigation when indicators fail.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: GPS vs. Map & Compass Navigation: Pivots act like automated GPS visual markers on a boat, whereas price and volume are traditional map-and-compass navigation.

facts.statement: A pennant pattern compresses price action like a tightly wound coiled spring, storing energy until it releases in an explosive breakout validated by volume.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: Coiled Spring: A pennant pattern contracting price action until stored energy releases in an explosive breakout.

facts.statement: Breakouts require heavy effort (high volume) to overcome dense congestion and pull away into a new trend, acting similarly to dragging a heavy object out of sticky quicksand.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: Dragging Someone Out of Quicksand: Breakouts require heavy effort (high volume) to overcome dense congestion and pull away into a new trend.

generalAssumptions: Market price manipulation is structurally transparent on the volume tape.
Effort versus result governs institutional capital movement.
